title: aidd common definitions
description: Shared vocabulary for every work item, typed document, and output of aidd. Tokens are snake_case and English.

aidd_version.description: The aidd release this record conforms to; the method and the toolkit share one version.

identity.description: Who: a typed identity `<type>:<value>`, or a platform login (`@user`, `@org/team`, or a bare login), which is a person unless schemas/agents.json names it an agent or a bot. `x-who` says whether each type names a person or an agent, and `x-meanings` what its value holds. Any form may be qualified with a tenant as `<tenant>:<identity>`, and a type's name is never a tenant's.

x-meanings.agent: `agent:<harness>/<model>`: an agent, as its commits' `Assisted-by` name it, such as `agent:claude-code/claude-opus-5-5`.
x-meanings.email: `email:<address>`: a person, by their address, unless schemas/agents.json names it an agent's commit address.
x-meanings.role: `role:<role>`: a role of the delivery team, such as `role:architect`, which an agent plays. Never a person.

approved_by.description: The person who said yes, in git's trailer form, like `Co-authored-by`: `Name <email>`, from their `git config user.name` and `git config user.email`. When that identity is a bot's or missing, it is the `Name <email>` or `@handle` the person gives. An Approver's `@handle`, `@org/team`, or `email:<address>` holds too. It names only who: the head, the action, or a delegation goes in the commit body or the decision record (`aidd records add`). `aidd validate` warns about another form, and about an agent or a bot.

glob.description: Repo-relative path glob. `*` stays inside one segment, `**` spans segments, a trailing `/` matches a directory.

command.description: Command vector, one argument per item. Never a shell string.

date.description: Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. The pattern rejects an impossible month or day (2026-13-01, 2026-04-31, 2026-02-30) with any validator; February 29 of a year that is not a leap year passes the pattern and fails only `format: date`, which aidd asserts but a stock validator may treat as an annotation.

url.description: The page the quote was copied from, read on the day in `checked`: a document or release page, never a bare homepage (its URL has a path).

quote.description: Copied exactly from that page. A registry entry quotes one full sentence (eight words or more, ending in `.`, `!`, or `?`), never the page title, that shows the edition or date. An extension or a library standard may quote the line that shows its pinned release, tag, commit, endpoint, or version. Anything less proves only that a page loaded, so `aidd eval standards` counts a registry entry as unconfirmed.

citation.description: Where a standard's source was read: the page, and the words on it. It makes a `checked` date a check and never a bare assertion. `aidd eval standards --online` fetches `url` again and looks for `quote`.

route.description: How much of the loop a change needs: advice from `aidd risk --paths`, never a control. An area can raise it, and the author may declare a higher one. ITIL 4 has normal and emergency changes; minor and major split normal by impact.

x-meanings.minor: Small and reversible, one Task, with no risk dimension. No Spec file: implement, verify, review, and Merge approval before the merge to the default branch.
x-meanings.normal: Everything that is not minor, major, or emergency. A Spec, with tests that fail on the base commit (red) and pass on head (green), and Spec approval where the profile asks for it.
x-meanings.major: Touches data, security, privacy, money, or compliance, edits an area that raises the route to major, or cannot be reverted. A Spec with more: a tech spec, a threat model for security, privacy, or data, a rollout plan, and an observe block.
x-meanings.emergency: Production is broken now and this change is the repair. Smoke tests still run, and the Spec and the review follow by `backfill_due`.

lane.description: The steps a route runs, derived from the route: fast for minor, spec for normal and major, emergency for emergency.

x-meanings.fast: The default: Implement ⟲ Verify -> Review -> Merge approval -> Merge -> Roll out, for a minor change.
x-meanings.spec: Specify -> Spec approval -> Implement ⟲ Verify -> Review -> Merge approval -> Merge -> Roll out, for normal and major changes, after an optional Plan.
x-meanings.emergency: Production repair: smoke tests, and the incident commander's yes before the merge and the deploy. The review and the Spec follow.

change_type.description: What kind of change this is, in Conventional Commits vocabulary. The type never raises the route: a risk dimension does, as `risk.dimensions` holds it and `aidd risk --dimension` declares it.

x-meanings.feat: New or changed behavior someone can see. Needs a new-behavior test on normal and major.
x-meanings.fix: Restores intended behavior. Needs a test that fails before the fix (red) and passes after (green).
x-meanings.refactor: Structure changes, behavior does not. Existing tests must stay green.
x-meanings.perf: Same behavior, different cost. Acceptance is a threshold.
x-meanings.docs: Documentation, content, or generated reference only.
x-meanings.build: Build system, packaging, developer tooling, third-party packages, or the infrastructure that runs the service. An infrastructure change also declares the dimension `availability`.
x-meanings.ci: Continuous integration or delivery pipelines and agent configuration.
x-meanings.chore: Housekeeping that changes no behavior: formatting, renames, cleanup.

status.description: Spec lifecycle status, stored in the Spec's front matter. The agent sets it as the work moves. Blocked is a flag (`waiting_on`), never a status.

x-meanings.draft: Being written, or sent back by a person's yes to `spec.revise`.
x-meanings.ready: Written. On a route that asks for Spec approval, the agent asked and waits for the answer.
x-meanings.approved: The person said yes to Spec approval, and the agent set `approved_by` and `approved_at`. Implementation may start.
x-meanings.in_progress: The agent implements the Spec's Tasks.
x-meanings.in_review: Verify and Review are clean on the head. The change waits for Merge approval.
x-meanings.done: Merged. Terminal, unless the observe window fails and the change rolls back.
x-meanings.rolled_back: The rollback ran, or the observe window failed (`outcome.rolled_back`, `outcome.observe_result: fail`). Terminal; Learn follows.
x-meanings.cancelled: A person stopped the work, or triage declined it. Terminal.

x-initial.when: you start the Spec (`aidd new spec`)

past_approval.means: At or past Spec approval. `approved_by` says who approved the Spec, and a test run decides by the base commit's copy of such a Spec.

before_implement.means: Before Implement: the Design stage, where the Spec's tests are expected to fail on the head.

specifying.means: Specify: the Spec is written, or waits for Spec approval. Work it is `blocked_by` holds Implement, never these.

implementing.means: Implement: the Tasks are built one by one, and Verify follows once every Task is done.

can_wait.means: Open work that can still be blocked. Once a Spec is in review, its work is built.

built.means: Every Task's work is built: the Spec is in review or past it.

started.means: Work on the Spec started, so the Intent that holds it is active.

ended.means: The work ended: it merged, was rolled back, or was cancelled. It counts toward its Intent's progress, and work that is `blocked_by` it may start.

landed.means: The change reached production, which a hypothesis is measured after.

asked.means: The Spec asked for approval, so the documents it folds into are due.

in_the_srs.means: The Spec's Acceptance is in the SRS.

acceptance_due.means: The Spec is in review or merged, so a record of manual acceptance is due.

without_triage.means: Work an agent suggested needs no person's triage here: nobody asked for approval yet, or the work was cancelled. At every other status, a person's triage must have accepted it.

x-transitions.when: the Spec validates, and you ask for Spec approval
the person says yes to Spec approval, and you commit it with an `Approved-by:` trailer of the same value (`references/spec.md`)
you say you go on, where `spec.approve` is `report` or `allow`: the Spec is approved, with `approved_at` and no `approved_by`, as under a delegation
the first commit in a Task's scope
Verify and Review are clean on the head, and you ask for Merge approval or open the PR/MR
a new push after that, until Verify is clean again
the person says yes to `spec.revise`, and you record what was wrong, when, and who said yes
the change is merged into the default branch, or under `batched` into `intent/<ID>`
the released change is rolled back, on the person's yes
a person stops the work, or declines it at triage

intent_status.description: An Intent's status. draft and active are derived from its slices; done and cancelled are a person's decision, stored. Blocked is a flag, never a status.

x-meanings.active: Derived: a slice has started (its Spec is in progress or later, or it merged).
x-meanings.done: Stored: a person closed it; `aidd status` suggests it once every slice is finished.

x-initial.when: you write the Intent (`aidd new intent`)

can_wait.means: Open work that can still be blocked.

started.means: A slice has started, so the Intent is active.

ended.means: A person closed it: done or cancelled.

needs_finished_children.means: Every slice and Spec of the Intent is finished.

x-transitions.when: a slice starts: its Spec is in progress or later, or it merged, and `aidd status` derives it
a person closes it on their yes, which `aidd status` suggests once every slice is finished
a person reopens it, because a slice is not finished
a person stops it, or records `go_no_go: no_go`

status_transition.description: One move of a work item's status, a row of a status table's `x-transitions`. A pair of statuses with no row is no move, and no status moves to itself. The statuses are words of the table's `enum`.

from.description: The statuses the move leaves. Each status of the list moves to `to` the same way.

who.description: Who moves it. `person`: a person decides it, and the agent records it on their yes. `agent`: the agent moves it on its own evidence.

when.description: What moves it, in the words the aidd skill's `references/state.md` shows.

requires.description: The front-matter fields of the item's own schema that the move leaves set: who decided, and when.

status_set.description: A named set of statuses that code reads as a fact about them, a row of a status table's `x-sets`. Each status is a word of the table's `enum`.

means.description: What it means for a status to be in the set.

statuses.description: The statuses in the set, in the order of the table's `enum`.

status_start.description: Where a new work item starts, the `x-initial` of a status table: the status it holds before any move, who starts it, and the words that say how. A missing status reads as this one.

status.description: The status a new item holds. A word of the table's `enum`.

who.description: Who starts it, as `who` of a move says.

when.description: What starts it, in the words the aidd skill's `references/state.md` shows.

slice.description: A planned Spec: one line in an Intent until its work starts. `aidd new spec <id>` writes the Spec from it and moves `blocked_by` and `delivery_team` into the Spec, so each fact keeps one owner. A slice carries no route: the route comes from the paths when its Spec is written.

id.description: The id its Spec takes, such as SPEC-32. Unique across the Intent's slices.

title.description: One line, the Spec's title to be.

blocked_by.description: The slices or Specs this one waits for before its work starts. `aidd validate` checks that they form no cycle.

delivery_team.description: The delivery team that delivers this slice, when it is not the Intent's: a key of the config's `delivery_teams`, which `aidd validate` checks.

repo.description: The repository that delivers this slice, when it is not this one. Its Spec sets `trace_id: <home>/<Intent id>`; aidd reads no other repository.

merged_in.description: The commit that merged a slice with no Spec file: one that routed minor, or one delivered in another repository.

drafted_in.description: The commit that holds a draft of its Spec, from before it became a slice line. `aidd new spec <id>` starts from that draft.

phase.description: An ordered group of an Intent's slices, with a date when a person names one. Phases that run side by side need no field: their slices are ready together. For a client engagement, a phase carries its invoicing hook.

id.description: A short key, such as P1.

name.description: A short name, such as "Walking skeleton".

due.description: The date the phase is committed for, only when a person names one.

finished_on.description: The day it finished, as a person records it (the client's acceptance). Never an agent.

amount.description: What is invoiced when it finishes, in `currency`.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 code, such as EUR or USD.

invoice_ref.description: The invoice's number once a person sends it.

slices.description: The phase's slices, in the order they merge.

type.description: The tracker's own word for the record, such as `initiative`, `epic`, or `story`.

id.description: The tracker's key, such as PORT-31.

tracker.description: Only when a tracker holds the record: the tracker's records this item links to, such as `{type: epic, id: PORT-31}`. The tracker owns its hierarchy and its order; the repository owns the words, the Spec, its tests, and every approval. aidd calls no tracker.

status_group.description: The group every status falls into, the same five for Specs, Intents, and proposals, so a board or a tracker can mirror any object by its group. `aidd status --json` gives each item's group.

x-meanings.backlog: Being written: a draft, or a proposal still being qualified.
x-meanings.unstarted: Written, waiting for approval or approved; nobody has started it.
x-meanings.started: Open work: being built, waiting for a person, or watched after release.
x-meanings.completed: Finished: done, rolled back (the work ended and Learn follows), or a proposal the addressee accepted.
x-meanings.cancelled: Stopped without delivery: cancelled, rejected, withdrawn, or a no-go.

blocked_by.description: The work items this one waits for before its work starts, by id. `aidd validate` checks that they form no cycle.

priority.description: How soon the work matters, for sorting the open work. Unset, it is inherited from the parent Intent, else medium; an emergency is always urgent. Bookkeeping: it never changes the route, and editing it needs no `spec.revise`.

x-meanings.urgent: Drop other work for it. Every emergency is urgent.

owner.description: The person driving the work, whom `aidd status` names as who acts. A person, never an agent or an agent account (`aidd validate` fails one). Bookkeeping: editing it needs no `spec.revise`, and it approves nothing.

confidence.description: Confidence in the assessment. Write it only as `low`, which stops the run. Unset, it is `high` while `open_questions` is empty and `medium` while it lists facts.

x-meanings.high: Every fact that could change the route is known. open_questions is empty.
x-meanings.medium: Some facts are missing, and none of them could change the route. List them, and go on.
x-meanings.low: A missing fact could change the route. Stop and ask.

next.description: A next step, the same in every output: what it is, with its stable `code` and who takes it when the output knows them.

code.description: A stable code, such as `spec.approve`, that a script may match on.

who.description: Who takes the step: an agent, a person, or nobody, when the step waits on other work or the work is finished.

person.description: For a step a person takes: who answers. The first approver for an approval, else the owner.

words.description: What a person types to their agent, or the command to run, to take the step. Absent for a step nobody takes, and for an item whose id is not a plain id (the schema's id pattern), because words hold no other text of the repository.

why.description: Why the step comes next, in one line, read from the data that owns the reason: the loop's lanes and decision rights in `schemas/roles.json`, or a schema's meaning. Absent where no data owns one, such as finished work.

step_code.description: A step `aidd status` can give, as the `code` of a next step: `<object>.<state>`, such as `spec.approve`, or one word. They run in the order a work item moves through them. `x-who` says who takes each step, and `x-meanings` what moves it on.

x-meanings.setup.missing: aidd is not set up in this repository: run `aidd init`
x-meanings.spec.emergency: an emergency Spec is open: restore service inside its scope first, then complete the Spec before its `backfill_due`
x-meanings.spec.triage: an agent suggested this work: a person triages it (accepted, declined, or snoozed) before anyone builds it
x-meanings.spec.blocked_by: the approved Spec waits for the work its `blocked_by` names: Implement starts when that work finishes
x-meanings.spec.blocked: the Spec names a wait in `waiting_on`: clear it and remove the entry, or re-plan
x-meanings.spec.planned: the Spec is planned, and nobody has started it: Specify writes it and its tests when its turn comes
x-meanings.spec.draft: the Spec and its tests are not finished: finish them, run `aidd validate`, then ask for Spec approval
x-meanings.spec.ask_approval: the Spec has no placeholder and `aidd validate` finds no error: set `status: ready`, then ask for Spec approval
x-meanings.spec.consumers: the revised Spec provides an interface that open Specs consume: finish it, then name those Specs and their owners in the Spec approval question
x-meanings.spec.approve: the Spec, its tests, and its design wait for a person's yes: the agent asked, and the person answers
x-meanings.spec.approved: the Spec is approved: implement it inside its Tasks' scope
x-meanings.spec.in_progress: the Spec is being built: finish its Tasks and get the tests green with `aidd test`
x-meanings.pr.merge: the built change waits for a person's Merge approval: they read the report, then say yes, or review the PR/MR
x-meanings.spec.done: the Spec is done: nothing to do
x-meanings.spec.outcome_due: the Spec's hypothesis is past due: measure its metric and record `outcome.result`
x-meanings.spec.rolled_back: the change was rolled back: write the postmortem
x-meanings.spec.cancelled: the Spec was cancelled: nothing to do
x-meanings.spec.task_person: a Task is assigned to a person: they do it, then record `done: true` on it
x-meanings.intent.agree: the Intent's goal and slices wait for a person's agreement: they read it, then say yes in the chat, and the agent records `agreed_by` and `agreed_at`
x-meanings.intent.slice: a slice of the agreed Intent is ready and has no Spec yet: write its Spec with `aidd new spec <id>`
x-meanings.intent.close: every slice of the Intent is finished: a person sets its status `done` (or `cancelled`)
x-meanings.exploration.open: an exploration waits for a person's pick: they read its options and its recommendation, then pick one in the chat
x-meanings.proposal.qualifying: a proposal waits for its go/no-go decision, which its decision maker records
x-meanings.proposal.drafting: the proposal is being drafted: `/aidd-team:propose`, then `aidd validate`
x-meanings.proposal.signed_off: the proposal is signed off: send it to its addressee, then record `outcome: submitted`
x-meanings.proposal.submitted: the proposal waits for its addressee to decide: record their answer in `outcome`
x-meanings.proposal.accepted: the proposal was accepted: plan the delivery work as an Intent and its phases
x-meanings.flag.overdue: a feature flag is past its `cleanup_due`: write the cleanup Spec that lists it in `removes_flags`
x-meanings.deprecation.overdue: a deprecation is past its `sunset`: write the removal Spec that lists it in `removes_deprecations`
x-meanings.nothing_open: nothing is open: describe the next change to the agent

stop_code.description: Why a run stopped, as the first word of a handoff note's `stopped_at`: `none` when the step is done, else the code the aidd skill's stop rule names, in the order of those rules. A note's `stopped_at` is one code, alone or with `: ` and a detail.

severity.description: `error`: the check fails. `warning`: something is likely wrong and the check still passes. `note`: for information.

finding.description: One thing a check found. A script matches `code`, never `message`. Outputs adopt this shape one by one.

code.description: A stable code, `<group>.<code>`, such as `delegate.delegation_review_due`. `schemas/findings.json` lists each one with its meaning and next step.

message.description: What was found, in a sentence a person reads.

path.description: The file the finding is about, repository-relative.

data.description: The facts behind the finding, such as the ids or paths it names.

error.description: The error a `--json` command prints on stdout before it exits 2, with the human text on stderr. Commands adopt it one by one.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape.

dimension.description: Blast-radius dimension, in words any role uses. `data`, `security`, `privacy`, `financial`, and `compliance` force major and name the specialist pool that reviews; every dimension rules out minor. Irreversibility is `risk.irreversible: true`, which also forces major.

x-meanings.data: Reads, writes, migrates, or deletes persistent or production data. Forces major; the `data` pool reviews.
x-meanings.security: Who can do what, and what can leak: authentication, authorization, roles, tokens, secrets, cryptography, attack surface. Forces major; the `security` pool reviews.
x-meanings.privacy: Personal data: collection, retention, sharing, deletion, consent. Forces major; the `privacy` pool reviews.
x-meanings.financial: Money moves or prices change: billing, payouts, pricing, ledgers, tax. Forces major; the `finance` pool reviews.
x-meanings.compliance: A legal, contractual, or regulatory control. Forces major; the `compliance` pool reviews.
x-meanings.availability: Can take a service down or degrade it: infrastructure, capacity, timeouts, limits. Rules out minor.
x-meanings.third_party: Adds or changes third-party code, services, images, or build inputs. Rules out minor.
x-meanings.cost: Can change spend materially: compute, storage, paid APIs, model tokens. Rules out minor.
x-meanings.performance: Can make a hot path slower or heavier: a new query, a loop over remote calls, a page asset, data that grows. Rules out minor; `aidd validate` warns until an Acceptance item states the budget and a test command covers it.

profile.description: The profile (schemas/profiles.json): its risk rules on top of the built-in ones, which set when the agent asks for Spec approval. `team` asks on more routes than `solo`. A lock freezes it; a child cannot raise it.

open_questions.description: Facts still unknown at assessment. Leave it out when none is.

summary.description: Blast radius in one or two sentences: who or what changes behavior.

dimensions.description: Every dimension the change touches. Empty means none.

irreversible.description: True when a revert does not restore the prior state, such as a destructive migration or an external side effect. True forces major.

residual.description: What stays true after release. `none` when nothing remains. A threat that stays is named by its id in the threat model, never restated.

monthly.description: What it costs to run each month at today's load, with its currency, such as `40 EUR`.

at_10x.description: The same at ten times today's load, such as `300 EUR`.

source.description: Where the numbers come from: `infracost diff`, a provider's pricing calculator, or a load test.

cost_estimate.description: What the change will cost to run, which the architect estimates in Specify: the one place for it. `aidd validate` warns on a Spec that changes infrastructure code, or whose risk names `cost`, and gives none. It also warns on a monthly estimate above `project.budget.max_infra_per_month`, the person's ceiling. Latency and availability belong in the SLO and `observe`.

risk.description: Blast radius: what changes, which dimensions it touches, whether a revert restores the prior state, what stays true after release, and what it costs to run.

runs_in.description: The folder the command runs in, as a path in the repository, such as `packages/api`. Omit it to run at the repository's top. `when_changed` and `report` stay relative to the top. A folder outside the repository, or one reached through a link, is refused.

new_behavior.description: True when this command proves new or fixed behavior. It must fail on the base commit (red) and pass on head (green).

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit. A timeout is a fail.

smoke.description: In the config's `tests`: part of the smoke set, the only repository commands an emergency change runs (with its own). When no command is marked, an emergency runs the whole suite.

reruns.description: How many more times a failing run on head runs again. Every run is kept in the evidence; a pass after a failure passes, marked flaky, and the flaky test is a finding. A red run on the base commit never runs again.

when_changed.description: Run and require this command only when a changed path matches. Omit to run it on every change.

command.description: The command that runs only the tests the runner relates to the changed files, through the runner's own mode, such as `[npx, jest, --passWithNoTests, --findRelatedTests, "{changed_paths}"]`. It holds `{changed_paths}`, an argument of its own that becomes each changed path from the command's folder, or `{base_commit}`, which becomes the commit the branch left the base at, or both. A command with neither, or another word in braces, fails the config's load.

sees.description: The paths the runner traces to their tests, from the repository's top, such as `src/**/*.ts`. A changed path the command covers that matches none of them, such as a lock file, a config, or a fixture, runs the full command.

related_tests.description: In the config's `tests`: how `aidd test --changed` runs only the tests related to the change. It runs `related_tests.command` when every changed path the command covers matches `sees`, is a file in the working tree, and lies inside the command's folder; else it runs the full command and says why. A full `aidd test`, `--require-green`, and every red run always run the full command. Omit it to run the full command under `--changed` too.

report.description: A JUnit XML report this command writes, as a path in the repository (pytest `--junitxml`, Vitest `--reporter=junit`, jest-junit, gotestsum, cargo-nextest, PHPUnit `--log-junit`). `aidd test` reads it after each run and records the test cases that failed, so a red run can be told from "no tests found". A missing, stale, or unreadable report is a finding. The exit code stays the evidence.

covers.description: In a Spec: the Acceptance items this command proves, by id (`A1`, `A2`, ...). Optional; once any command declares it, `aidd validate` warns about an Acceptance item no command covers, and about an id the Acceptance section does not have.

test_command.description: One test command. Exit 0 is the only pass.

files.description: The acceptance test files, and the configuration they run through. Frozen at Spec approval: changing them after is `spec.revise`, which asks. Never inside a Task's scope, which holds the unit tests written with the code. A test section of `pyproject.toml` or `package.json` is frozen by itself as `<path>#<dotted key>`, such as `pyproject.toml#tool.pytest` or `package.json#scripts.test`, so a dependency bump is not a change to the tests.

items.description: A Spec's command. It has no `related_tests`: a Spec's own tests run in full whenever they run.

commands.description: Commands the runner executes. Exit 0 is the only pass.

tests.description: How the change is proven: the test files and the commands that run them.

commander.description: The incident commander, a human. Named before the repair starts.

incident.description: The incident's ticket or page id, such as INC-481: what the repair answers, and what the post-incident review and the backfill Spec link. Required on an emergency change.

backfill_due.description: Date the postmortem and the backfill Spec are due. From the day after, until `outcome.learn_ref` records the review, `aidd validate` fails.

emergency.description: The incident an emergency change repairs. Required on the emergency route.

not_applicable.description: Why nothing runs to watch after release, such as "a CLI and its docs: no running service". It takes the place of the other fields, so the person asked for approval sees the reason.

signals.description: Dashboards, SLOs, or queries a human watches.

window.description: How long to watch, such as 30m, 24h, or 7d.

rollback_trigger.description: The condition that starts the rollback.

observe.description: What to watch after release, for how long, and when to roll back.

repo_path.description: A plain repo-relative file path: no leading `./` or `/`, no backslashes, no wildcards.

sha.description: A 40- or 64-character lowercase hex git object ID.

red_green.description: green runs on head; red runs the head's tests against the base code.

goal.description: The measurable goal of an Intent.

term.description: A word the aidd skill, the CLI's messages, and the docs use that no other data names, with the first sentence of the glossary's meaning (docs/GLOSSARY.md owns the whole meaning, and a test holds the two together).

x-meanings.evidence: `.aidd/evidence/evidence.json`, which `aidd test` writes: the exit code of each command on the head, and of each new-behavior command on the base, bound to the head commit.
x-meanings.frozen: A test that Spec approval froze: an acceptance test, or a test file listed in the Spec's `tests.files`.
x-meanings.headless: A session with nobody at the prompt, such as CI, a cloud session, or a scheduled run.
x-meanings.limit: A named number that changes what aidd decides or shows, such as the retries a Task gets or the paths an answer lists.
x-meanings.method: How aidd works: the loop, the routes, the risk rules, Conventional Commits types, and `Assisted-by:`.
x-meanings.recall: A search of what the team already wrote: the records, the Specs, the ADRs, the glossary, the product brief, the improvement log, and the commit subjects.
x-meanings.stop code: The first word of a handoff note's `stopped_at`, which says why the run stopped, such as `none`, `ask`, or `retries`, alone or with `: ` and a detail.
x-meanings.stop rule: One condition in the aidd skill's Stop and hand back list, such as an `ask` that waits for the person or a third failed retry.
x-meanings.work item: A Spec, an Intent, or a proposal (`spec`, `intent`, `proposal`): a file with a status group and a next step in `aidd status`.
